name: 47782-sparseprefix-4b-1gpu
hardware: 1x NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3 (one GPU of an a3 node, --gres=gpu:1).
parallelism: TP=1, PP=1, DP=1. One in-process engine; no context parallelism, KV connector, offload tier, router or speculative decoding.
architecture: Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration, bf16, 4B params, ~9.3 GB of weights; hybrid text stack of 8 full-attention and 24 linear-attention layers, plus a vision tower this text-only workload never invokes.
load_profile: concurrent (closed loop), streams=10, warmup 10% and cooldown 10% both pinned to `mode: requests`, 300 requests bounded, safety_seconds 1800.
workload: shared-prefix repetition, single turn, text only: 20 distinct 6000-token prefixes, each request one of them followed by a 2000-token request-unique body and 100 generated tokens, greedy, 300 requests, driven in-process through guidellm's `vllm_python` backend.
purpose: A knowledge-base assistant answering single-turn questions over 20 shared 6000-token briefs, ten concurrent users, one GPU.
launch:
# 47782-sparseprefix-4b-1gpu -- the launch config, in `vllm serve --config` form.
# One setting of this item cannot be written as an engine argument and is declared in
# `env.yaml` instead: VLLM_PREFIX_CACHE_RETENTION_INTERVAL=0.

model: Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B
tensor-parallel-size: 1

# 8000 prompt tokens + 100 generated + chat template fit in one context and one step's budget.
max-model-len: 8192
max-num-batched-tokens: 8192

# NOT a restatement of a default: this engine leaves prefix caching off for hybrid checkpoints,
# so on this one it is opt-in and deleting the key serves the workload with no reuse at all.
enable-prefix-caching: true
enable-chunked-prefill: true

# What the engine resolves for this checkpoint anyway; pinned so the file states it.
mamba-cache-mode: align

# Platform necessity, not a tuning choice. The FlashInfer GDN prefill kernel this engine picks by
# default on SM90 is JIT-compiled on first use, and in this venv that compile raises
# `TypeError: 'function' object is not subscriptable` and kills EngineCore before a single request
# completes. Triton/FLA is the engine's own suggested alternative and takes the same arguments.
# See configs/note.md.
gdn-prefill-backend: triton
